title: Mastering the Ring: ICRS & CAIRS in Corneal Ectasia
summary: A comprehensive clinical guide to Intracorneal Ring Segments (ICRS) and Corneal Allogenic Intrastromal Ring Segments (CAIRS). This poster covers biomechanical principles, topography-guided planning, and the transition from synthetic implants to allogenic tissue for advanced keratoconus management.

sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: Intracorneal Ring Segments (ICRS) are PMMA medical devices implanted into the deep corneal stroma to flatten the central cornea and reduce refractive error in ectatic diseases. Corneal Allogenic Intrastromal Ring Segments (CAIRS) represent a paradigm shift, using donor corneal tissue instead of synthetic PMMA to improve biocompatibility and allow for treatment in thinner corneas (pachymetry < 400μm).

sections.title: Biomechanical Principles
content: Step 1: Barraquer's Thickness Law - Adding volume to the corneal periphery flattens the center.
Step 2: Arc-Shortening Effect - The ring displaces the lamellae, creating a 'tenting' effect that pulls the apex down.
Step 3: Flattening Ratio - Proportional to the thickness of the segment and inversely proportional to its diameter.
Step 4: Remodeling - Long-term stabilization of the corneal collagen matrix.

sections.title: ICRS vs. CAIRS: The Allogenic Advantage

rows: Slightly slower due to tissue integration

sections.title: Topography: The Planning Blueprint
content: Axial Map: Identifies the 'Steepest Meridian' for incision placement.
Elevation Map: Crucial for detecting the cone apex (Posterior elevation is more sensitive).
Pachymetry Map: Must identify the thinnest point along the proposed 5mm/6mm/7mm track.
Coma Symmetry: Higher-order aberrations (HOAs) guide segment asymmetry (e.g., thicker segment inferiorly for inferior cones).
Incision Axis: Usually placed at the steep axis of the 'Coma' or the steepest keratometric meridian.

sections.title: Surgical Contraindications
content: Central Corneal Scarring (prevents visual improvement)
History of Hydrops (ruptured Descemet's membrane)
Pachymetry < 300μm at the track site (for ICRS)
Very Steep K (>65-70D typically poor prognosis)
Active Ocular Infection or Severe Atopy
Unrealistic Patient Expectations

branches: Arc Length (90° to 340°): Smaller arcs treat astigmatism; longer arcs treat sphere.
Diameter (5mm, 6mm, 7mm): Smaller diameter = more powerful effect.

sections.title: The CAIRS Procedure Steps
content: Step 1: Tissue Preparation - Use a double-blade trephine or FS laser to cut a 10-12mm donor ring.
Step 2: De-epithelialization of donor tissue (if using fresh).
Step 3: FS Laser Tunneling - 80% depth at the thinnest point of the track.
Step 4: Insertion - Using 'Push-Pull' or 'Sinskey' technique to guide allogenic tissue into the tunnel.
Step 5: Centration - Centering based on the Purkinje reflex or pupillary center.

content.explanation: R: Refraction (Stable?); I: Imaging (Topography/Pachymetry); N: Nomogram (Arc/Thickness); G: Gauging depth (80%); S: Scarring (Check central clarity).

branches: Late: Segment Migration, Extrusion (PMMA > CAIRS), Epithelial Ingrowth.
Visual: Halos/Glare (especially with 5mm rings), Induced astigmatism.

sections.title: Recent Advances & Landmark Studies
content: Soosan Jacob et al. (2018): Introduced CAIRS as a safer alternative for thin corneas.
Athens Protocol: Combining ICRS with CXL (Cross-linking) for simultaneous flattening and stabilization.
Topography-Guided CAIRS: Customizing tissue thickness based on focal steepening.
Asymmetric Segments: Using 'tapered' or variable thickness segments (Keraring AS) to treat asymmetric cones.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls for Fellows
content: Always aim for 70-80% corneal depth; shallow placement leads to extrusion.
For CAIRS, use 10.0 nylon sutures if the incision is wide, though often self-sealing.
The 'Coma Axis' is more reliable for incision placement than the 'K-Axis' in highly irregular corneas.
Inform patients that rings are for 'functional' vision improvement, not necessarily to eliminate glasses.

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: Diagnosis: Progressive Keratoconus with contact lens intolerance.
Selection: Pachymetry > 450μm? Use ICRS. Pachymetry < 400μm? Consider CAIRS.
Procedure: Femtosecond laser tunnel creation (Gold Standard).
Follow-up: Day 1, Week 1, Month 1, Month 3. Monitor for CXL need.
